title: The Many-to-Many Relationship
summary: Covers associative entities, relational mapping of many-to-many relationships, three-table joins, existence tests, relational division, and set operations.

concepts.title: Associative entities
concepts.summary: A many-to-many relationship is resolved through an associative entity connected to each original entity by a one-to-many relationship.

concepts.title: Facts about a relationship
concepts.summary: Attributes that describe a pairing belong on the associative entity because they describe neither participating entity alone.

concepts.title: Weak entities and composite identifiers
concepts.summary: An associative or weak entity may rely on a related entity's identifier plus a local value to form a unique composite identifier.

sections.title: Creating a relational database with an m:m relationship

concepts.title: Mapping many-to-many relationships
concepts.summary: The associative table contains foreign keys for both related tables, with a primary key chosen to identify each association.

concepts.title: Three-table joins
concepts.summary: Querying both sides of a many-to-many relationship joins each original table to the associative table with a separate matching condition.

concepts.title: EXISTS and NOT EXISTS
concepts.summary: EXISTS tests whether at least one related row satisfies a condition; NOT EXISTS succeeds only when no such row exists.

concepts.title: Relational division
concepts.summary: Questions asking which targets relate to every source can be expressed through nested non-existence tests or equivalent grouped counts.

concepts.title: Set operations
concepts.summary: UNION combines rows from either compatible result, while INTERSECT retains rows present in both compatible results.
